description: Discriminator: after the executor's timeout path enqueues a blocked instance, does handing that entry to the recovery entry actually start a recovery (a preparing record with a Prepare on the wire)? Prefix: the harness blocks one row with the package's own constructor, starts the real executor goroutine, waits for the enqueue, then calls startRecoveryForInstance with the enqueued coordinates and reports the record's bookkeeping and the bytes emitted. Controls: the first prerequisite prints the blocked record and its watermarks, the second prints the enqueue with the waiting time, and the result prints whether the recovery is preparing, how many bytes were sent and how many self replies the bookkeeping holds.

harness.description: In-package Go test that drives the executor timeout, then the recovery entry, and reports whether recovery started.
semantic_changes: harness-only scaffolding: the Replica is constructed in-package, the executor goroutine is started directly and the recovery entry is called with the enqueued coordinates instead of by the run loop
peer writers are buffers kept by the harness so the emitted Prepare is observable

legality.derivation: The enqueued instance is exactly what the run loop hands to the recovery entry in production, and the entry is the implementation's own.
legality.applicability: One blocked row, executor running, then one recovery entry call.
unresolved: the run loop's own consumption of the channel is replaced by the harness

grounding.derivation: The event reports whether the record is preparing and whether a Prepare left the replica, which is the observable of a started recovery.
grounding.applicability: The entry was called with the enqueued coordinates.

observable_properties.description: An instance the timeout path enqueued must leave the replica in a preparing recovery state.

uncertainties: the harness calls the recovery entry itself rather than letting the run loop consume the channel
one blocked row and one enqueue are exercised
